# Understanding Cairn Mechanics

## Core Concept: The Pulse (Rule C1)
A pulse increases a cairn's height, but the amount added depends on the current height. You add the stride plus a bonus equal to how many complete strides fit into the current height. This creates a feedback loop where taller cairns grow faster.

## Repeated Pulses (Rule C2)
When pulsing multiple times, you must recalculate after each pulse. You can't use shortcuts or assume the bonus stays constant. As the cairn grows taller, each successive pulse adds more because more complete strides fit into the larger height.

## Leaks (Rule C3)
After pulsing, a leak removes marks proportionally based on the new (pulsed) height. The leak size determines how many marks drain away—one mark per complete leak-size units in the height. The key is that leaks apply *after* the pulse, not before.

## Finding Original Heights (Rule C4)
You can work backwards from a final height to find starting heights by undoing pulses one at a time. Since pulses only increase height in one direction, each final height has exactly one original starting height that produces it.

## Draining Cycles (Rule C5)
Draining combines pulses with fixed losses repeatedly. The cairn empties when the drain exceeds what a pulse adds. Since pulses get smaller as height decreases, you must track each cycle individually—simple division won't predict when emptying occurs.

## Merging Cairns (Rule C6)
Merging two cairns creates a new height using weighted portions from each, plus a tether contribution. The tether acts as a multiplier of the shorter cairn divided by 10, making it essential to the final merged height.
